sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax or registry distinction relevant to the SCSp)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage, strongly harmonized with EU directives; commercial entities governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, and the Luxembourg Civil Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Income Tax Treaty (signed 1996, amended by 2009 Protocol)
Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty network
EU Arbitration Convention 90/436/EEC on transfer pricing adjustment disputes
Multilateral Instrument (MLI) covered agreements applicable to Luxembourg treaty re-invoicing and commissionaire structures

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended in 2023 following CJEU C-37/20 and C-601/20 restricting public access; Law of 12 July 2013 creating the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp), now codified in Articles 901-1 to 901-17 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; EU Regulation 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: SCSp constitutive deed: notarial instrument (acte notarie de societe en commandite speciale) or private written partnership agreement in notarized form for RCSL publication
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (notaire) appointed by the partners, assisted by the drafting law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) for foreign certificate of incorporation and power-of-attorney documents originating in Apostille Contracting States; mandatory Consular Legalization for documents originating in non-Apostille jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of non-opposition to company name (certificat de non-opposition)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCSL) via the eJustice portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; internally generated administrative act of the Luxembourg registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration file (declaration des beneficiaires effectifs) with certified identification documents of each UBO holding 25% or more of the partnership interests
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner of the SCSp, supported by notarized or consular-certified copies of passports, proof of address, and corporate charters
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization depending on the country of issuance of each underlying identification document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of domiciliation and registered office acceptance issued by the Luxembourg registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: CSSF-supervised professional domiciliation company (Law of 31 May 1999 on domiciliation companies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal administrative document; notarized signature specimen of the general partner required for RCSL filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing screening of all general partners, limited partners, authorized signatories, and material beneficiaries against: (1) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Council Regulation 269/2014); (2) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions; (3) OFAC SDN and primary sanctions lists; (4) Luxembourg national sanctions list maintained by the Ministry of Finance; (5) CSSF AML/CFT guidelines and the CSSF-Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) goAML filing obligations; and (6) FATF high-risk jurisdiction call lists. PEP detection applies the definition in Article 1 of the Law of 12 November 2004 (political exposure, family members, close associates). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any UBO resident in a FATF-flagged jurisdiction, for sanctioned trade corridors, or where the re-invoicing chain involves split payments through third-country intermediaries. Negative screening hits require escalation to the CRF and a written suspicious transaction alert before incorporation proceeds.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: Dossier filed with the RBE is accessible only to the Luxembourg authorities (CSSF, CRF, AED tax administration, notaries, lawyers, auditors) and to persons demonstrating a legitimate interest; no public bulk access is available after the 2023 transparency reform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCSL), online filing via the eJustice portal at www.lbr.lu and www.ejustice.public.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; French, German, and Luxembourgish are the official register languages. Non-Latin script names (Arabic, Cyrillic, Chinese, Greek) must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by a French or German translation of the company purpose. The legal form suffix 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or 'SCSp' is mandatory; suffixes implying public limited companies (SA, Sarl, SCA, SE) are prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, Banking, Credit Institution (requires prior CSSF authorization)
Assurance, Reassurance, Insurance (requires CAA regulatory license)
Fonds, FCP, SICAV, SICAF, RAIF, SIF (regulated fund designations require CSSF approval)
Bourse, Stock Exchange, Trading Platform, Clearing House (regulated market terminology)
Luxembourg, Luxembourgish, National, State, Commune, Municipal (misleading public or sovereign affiliation requires ministerial approval)
Titrisation, Securitization (triggering the Securitization Law of 22 March 2004 and CSSF authorization)
Paiement, Payment Institution, E-money, Cryptocurrency (reserved licensed activities without which incorporation is rejected)
Groupement d'Interet Economique and other statutorily reserved designations
Any token creating confusion with an existing RCSL-registered corporate name or a protected trademark in Luxembourg
Words contrary to public order, public decency, or Luxembourg Criminal Code provisions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Step 1: file a preliminary name availability search via the eJustice portal; Step 2: submit the formal application for the certificat de non-opposition to the LBR, receiving either issuance or a reasoned refusal; Step 3: if refused, the notary or any interested party may request a detailed written justification from the LBR within 15 days; Step 4: administrative reconsideration by letter to the Director of LBR within one month; Step 5: judicial appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within two months of the refusal notification, using summary proceedings (refere) where time is material; Step 6: if the name is sensitive due to regulated tokens, a parallel application for prior CSSF or ministerial approval must be submitted before re-filing. A refused name may be re-filed after alteration of the offending token; the negative certificate is automatically annulled if the constitutive deed is not registered before expiry of the 60-day validity window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partly permissible with material limitations. The SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg; the Law of 31 May 1999 permits domiciliation through a licensed domiciliation agent to satisfy the formal address requirement. However, for an ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing hub, the Luxembourg tax administration (AED) and the RCSL require substantive local presence: local decision-making, board or management meeting minutes in Luxembourg, local administrative support, a Luxembourg bank account, and transfer pricing documentation consistent with OECD substance requirements. A purely virtual office without local accounting, management, and banking substance will be treated as an artificial arrangement, attracting circular-economy reclassification, BEPS/ATAD penalties, and possible refusal of Luxembourg tax residence. The recommended model is a licensed domiciliation company plus a substance-servicing partnership administrator.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 30% to 35% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection within the first three financial years where the SCSp records low personnel headcount, high-volume re-invoicing, and transactions with APAC or Eastern European counterparties. The AED, CCSS (social security authority), and the RCSL perform randomized field visits targeting domiciliation addresses hosting more than 20 entities; a standalone commercial address with visible files and local administration materially reduces inspection risk.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed preparation and execution for the SCSp constitutive act
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (tarif de notaire) for partnerships without immovable contributions; prevailing notarial market range USD 2,100 to 3,300

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Limited partnership agreement (LPA) drafting with governing law, profit-split, and re-invoicing clauses
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (cabinet d'avocats) registered with the Luxembourg Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a cross-border trade intermediary LPA with re-invoicing charge mechanics and dispute resolution provisions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL statutory inscription fee (depot au registre de commerce et des societes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official LBR fee schedule for registration of new legal persons

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RESA / LBR publication and electronic gazette fee (publication des actes)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: LBR / Recueil Electronique des Societes et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-line statutory publication tariff; average 10 to 20 lines per constitutive deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official administrative fee for issuance of the negative name certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE beneficial ownership registration filing and UBO dossier preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE) / Ministere de la Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutorily free first filing; no government tariff applies

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT KYC and UBO identification piercing dossier (source of funds, chain of control chart, FATCA/CRS classification)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for medium-risk re-invoicing entity; 4 to 6 hours at USD 190 to 275 per hour

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions list automated screening subscriptions and audit trail
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed screening software vendor / registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual per-entity license benchmark for a single legal entity with up to three UBOs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blend of statutory apostille fees (USD 20 to 120 per document), consular legalization tariffs (USD 50 to 150 per document), and courier costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of foreign documents into French or German for LBR and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn / certified translator (traducteur jure) accredited in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page statutory rate; average 8 to 12 pages of constitutional documents and UBO identification translations

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 905-1 to 905-24 concerning the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); protocol provisions of the Luxembourg Civil Code for partnership contracts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Ministry of Justice
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of association (statuts) executed before a notary or by private deed, filed with the RCS for legal personality registration and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital; SCSp requires no minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account. Contributions may be cash, in-kind, or industry, and must be fully subscribed by the partners as described in the articles of association.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: This pro-forma resolution is adopted by the general partner of the proposed Société en Commandite Spéciale. RESOLVED: 1. All partnership interests are subscribed by the initial general and limited partners, and the contributions set out in the articles are accepted in full. 2. The registered office of the partnership is fixed at [address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, as its principal administrative seat. 3. [Name] is appointed manager, with authority to open bank accounts, sign trade documents, and carry out ordinary re-invoicing transactions. 4. Counsel and the notary are instructed to file the articles with the RCS and complete the RESA publication. 5. Any ancillary acts to perfect incorporation are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS pre-registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit two proposed company names through the LBR online platform for negative clearance. Upon approval, obtain the name reservation certificate and proceed directly to drafting the notarial deed. The name must clearly distinguish the partnership, and the SCSp suffix must appear in the corporate name.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of the general partner and initial partners
Proof of registered office address (lease or occupancy agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name immediately. If the reservation is refused for formal defects, file a corrected application within 15 days. A formal appeal may be addressed to the Luxembourg Business Registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Civil Law Notary (notaire), Luxembourg district
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association in French or German (or English with certified translation) containing the SCSp's name, registered office, corporate purpose, contribution amounts, classes of partnership interests, management authority of the general partner, and duration. Ensure the document is executed before a notary for registration and publication purposes; if private deed is used, notarization is still required before RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association in final form
General partner consent and appointment declaration
Manager acceptance letter if not the general partner
Registered office consent letter from the property owner
Identity and tax numbers of all initial partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting defects by notarial addendum before filing. If execution is incomplete, re-execute before the same notary. No re-notarization is required if substantive law is satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed notarial deed, the RCS filing application, and all statutory annexes with the RCS. Upon validation, the RCS assigns a registration number and entry is made in the trade register, conferring legal personality from the date of registration. Pay the applicable registration fee upon filing.
required_dossiers: RCS filing form (Module C or applicable combined form)
Identity documents of the manager and general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query, submit corrected documents and explanations within 15 days. If the query concerns missing annexes, file the omitted dossiers immediately. Paid priority review is available for time-sensitive transactions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) through the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration, the registry automatically transmits the incorporation data to RESA for legal publication. Verify the published extract and ensure consistency with the filed articles. The publication evidences statutory disclosure to third parties; it is not constitutive of legal personality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, request a publication status certificate from the RCS. If the published text contains errors, file an erratum or rectification request with the RCS within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if employing staff; Commercial Bank for account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA) using the RCS extract and articles. Register for corporate income tax and municipal business tax through the direct tax administration. Open a business bank account after completing KYC/AML due diligence. No separate license is required for re-invoicing activities.
required_dossiers: Identity and address of each beneficial owner
AML/source-of-funds statement for bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the VAT application, provide corrected beneficial-owner declarations and business purpose explanations within 15 days. If the bank requests additional KYC documents, submit them promptly; otherwise request a formal refusal letter to exercise legal remedies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale de l'industrie et de l'innovation), Luxembourg — only if industrial production is later added; not relevant for a re-invoicing hub
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — general trade intermediation and re-invoicing are not licensed activities under Luxembourg commercial law; no manufacturing permit is required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency), Ministry of Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical production, warehousing, industrial emissions, or pollutant discharge; no environmental impact assessment or registration is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — desk-based commercial re-invoicing generates no wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous waste. If future warehousing is introduced, waste management plans and applicable emissions thresholds under Luxembourg environmental law must be reassessed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Registered office fire safety certification must be obtained from the landlord or building owner under Luxembourg fire-safety standards. Structural load inspections are not applicable to office-only occupancy. Workplace clearance under the Labour Code may be required if staff are employed, subject to inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct and corporate income tax matters; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and stamp taxes; Administration des douanes et accises for customs and excise procedures. Central digital access portals: myGuichet.lu, guichet.public.lu, the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) e-registration portal, and the SUD electronic customs declaration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File the SCSp with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) through an appointed Luxembourg registered office/agent, obtaining the RCS matricule and the national business identification number. Step 2: Open the tax dossier (numéro de dossier) with the ACD/AEDT, which produces the Luxembourg corporate TIN for the entity. Step 3: Submit the VAT registration application to the AEDT Service de la TVA using the standard non-established taxable person procedure, including powers of attorney, identity documents of partners and managers, proof of the re-invoicing business activity and expected turnover; a non-resident entity without a Luxembourg permanent establishment may register directly for VAT or, when necessary, appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative. The Luxembourg VAT ID follows the format LU + 8 digits. Registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply is made in Luxembourg, and no registration fee is levied.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The SCSp is a special limited partnership without separate legal personality and is fiscally transparent for direct tax purposes: profits are attributed and taxed directly at partner level (corporate partners are subject to corporate income tax and municipal business tax; individual partners to personal income tax), while the SCSp itself is not a CIT or municipal business tax taxpayer. For VAT, the SCSp is treated as a taxable person where all partners are VAT taxable persons; mixed-partner structures are analysed at partner/co-ownership level. The activity is ordinary territorial nexus-based; no special tax-exempt zone is engaged.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election regime exists in Luxembourg; tax transparency of the SCSp is a statutory attribute rather than an elective classification. Partnerships nevertheless remain subject to hybrid mismatch analysis under LIR Articles 168ter and 168quater (ATAD 1 and 2) and OECD BEPS Action 2 outcomes, including reverse-hybrid and import mismatch rules. For VAT, AEDT interpretative practice permits the SCSp to be treated as a VAT taxable person where all partners are taxable persons, effectively an optional consolidation of partner VAT status into the partnership; there is no US-style 338/168 or UK section 59A analogue.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) — EU-harmonised value added tax under Council Directive 2006/112/EC and the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (LVD), administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover small-business exemption threshold for Luxembourg-established businesses under Article 57 LVD. Non-resident re-invoicing intermediaries making taxable supplies in Luxembourg must register for VAT from the first euro and cannot benefit from the SME exemption; intra-Community distance sales and acquisition thresholds also trigger registration in the relevant Member State.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector entities and must be exchanged in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format through a certified PEPPOL access point, with central procurement data submitted via the InMyBX electronic platform. There is no general B2B real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), API data-streaming or digital stamping regime currently in force; B2B e-invoicing remains optional provided authenticity of origin and integrity of content are ensured. Luxembourg is aligning with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) proposals, which will introduce additional cross-border B2B e-invoicing obligations in the future.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% VAT) may be claimed under Article 51 et seq. LVD for: (i) supplies of goods physically exported outside the EU, provided the goods leave EU territory within three months of dispatch and the supplier holds complete export evidence; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods where the customer supplies a valid Luxembourg or other Member State VAT identification number and goods are dispatched to another Member State, subject to EC Sales Lists, VIES and Intrastat reporting; and (iii) certain B2B services that are treated as supplied outside Luxembourg under the place-of-supply rules of Article 14 LVD, including re-invoicing and commissionaire services rendered by the SCSp to a non-EU principal and services ancillary to export transactions. The 0% rate is recorded in Box 5 of the periodic VAT return; the zero-rating cannot be applied merely because the customer is non-resident and the exporter must preserve the full documentary chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration — Single Administrative Document or electronic SUD/CDS export declaration, including the declaration number and proof of exit confirmation
Transport evidence — CMR waybill, bill of lading (B/L), air waybill (AWB) or multimodal transport document depending on mode of carriage
Commercial documentation — sales contract or purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin and proof of title transfer

Payment and FX proceeds evidence — SWIFT MT103/telegraphic transfer credit advice, bank FX repatriation credit note, or an Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing foreign currency remittance to the SCSp bank account
Proof of physical exit from EU territory — customs exit confirmation (EUREX/NSTI records), officially stamped transport documents, or third-party warehouse/carrier certification
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT rigorously audits zero-rated export claims and coordinates with ACD reviews of economic substance and beneficial ownership. Incomplete or inconsistent export, transport or remittance evidence enables retrospective VAT reassessment for up to five years (ten years in cases of fraud), recalculating VAT at the standard 17% rate with default interest at 0.6% per commenced month, late-payment penalties, administrative fines generally ranging between 10% and 20% of the underdeclared tax, and disallowance of corresponding input VAT credits. Fraudulent export documentation attracts criminal tax-evasion penalties, including fines up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to five years, with joint and several liability of managers. The 180-day proceeds-repatriation benchmark supports the substance and economic-effect analysis of the SCSp re-invoicing trade; sustained non-repatriation may additionally trigger transfer-pricing recharacterisation and deemed distribution treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the National Central Bank, together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the supervisory authority for banks and payment institutions within the Luxembourg financial centre. EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital are directly applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a eurozone jurisdiction with full and unrestricted capital and current account convertibility under Articles 63-65 TFEU. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements, and no mandatory conversion or repatriation restrictions for trade proceeds. Profit remittance by an SCSp is tax-free at the partnership level given its fiscally transparent status, and payments to non-resident partners are generally made without Luxembourg withholding tax provided the applicable conditions under Luxembourg domestic law and relevant double tax treaties are met.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender regime exists in Luxembourg. Receipts from export activities can be retained in any currency or converted at the freely negotiated market rate. The only compliance requirement is indirect statistical reporting to the BCL for balance-of-payments purposes and, where applicable, EU customs reporting, but no mandatory conversion ratio or timing is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Trade Settlement Account with segregated capital escrow sub-ledger

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Account and separate Escrow Account
Operational Account with Foreign Currency Deposit Facilities
Operational Account with FX and liquidity management suite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High practical viability for ancillary transactions, but not for core treasury. Passported or Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 can operate digital accounts for an SCSp, restricted to e-money issuance and payment services. Legal constraints include the inability of an EMI to grant credit or accept deposits, the absence of deposit guarantee coverage on e-money float, and the need for a separate Tier-1 bank account for LC operations or large trade settlements. Such EMIs are therefore suitable for low-value payables, FX conversion, and fast cross-border XT transfers, not as a standalone liquidity clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of at least one authorised partner, director, and the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) is the standard requirement at account opening. Most Luxembourg banks require a face-to-face meeting in Luxembourg or at a recognised bank branch abroad. Remote videoconference onboarding is available only in very limited cases such as an existing long-term core banking relationship, an introducing central bank, or a regulated professional intermediary with direct verification. A pure remote onboarding mandate for a non-resident SCSp is rarely accepted and the account would initially be restricted to zero-value activity until physical attestation is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp organised as a shell-like limited partnership without visible local substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office agreement, local corporate administrator, secretary and accounting function, physical office lease, list of actual directors with residence/address, business plan, invoice and contract flow, prior year financial statements, tax registrations, and a detailed group structure chart with commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Re-invoicing business with identical goods being bought and sold across borders without value addition.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master trading agreements, purchase orders, underlying end-customer contracts, proof of risk transfer, shipping and insurance documentation, intercompany transfer pricing policy with benchmarking, and board minutes approving margin and risk transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital contributions involving intra-group financing or crypto-derived wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements of the contributing entity for the last 12 months, loan agreement or equity investment documentation, audited financial statements of the parent, commercial registry extracts, VAT and tax filings, and sworn asset declarations if required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dealings with high-risk jurisdictions or transactions routed through concentration accounts in third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Economic substance justification, end-beneficiary identification, beneficial ownership registry extraction, sanctions screening evidence, downstream KYC files, and independent legal opinion on the commercial operation of the SCSp.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for subscription and capital contributions: transfer via SWIFT MT103 from the parent/contributing entity to the Luxembourg operational account, with the payment referencing the SCSp name, fully paid subscription and the applicable purpose code under the BCL statistical classification (direct investment equity or intra-group capital). Before the wire, the bank compliance team must receive: executed subscription agreement, capital contribution resolution, notice of intent, ultimate beneficial owner identification, source-of-wealth documents, and evidence of the entry in the Luxembourg Register of Commercial and Companies for the SCSp. Intermediary banks must be EU-approved and not blacklisted; the beneficiary account number must match the op account exactly.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for open account supplier payments and commercial letters of credit (UCP600) executed through SWIFT MT700/MT707 where the beneficiary requires LC protection. For EUR instant disbursements within SEPA, the XT_Transfer format can be used via the bank's real-time payment rail. The chosen rail must carry the proper purpose code, reference the underlying invoice, and be supported by transport documents, packing lists and invoice copies retained for AML/FI checks. Both TT_Wire and Swift_LC rails are employed for re-invoicing settlement, while XT_Transfer is reserved for low-value operative payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and major convertible currencies covering documented underlying trade flows, subject to a master netting or ISDA credit support annex.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for hedge settlement risk in restricted or illiquid currencies not freely deliverable in Luxembourg, permitted only with bank-executed underlying exposure.
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for long-term intra-group loan receivables and to align funding currencies of the SCSp, limited to systemic hedging, not speculative trading.

Vanilla FX call and put options for hedging forecast re-invoicing receivables and payables, provided the options are duly documented and within the treasury risk policy approved by partner/capital owners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RBE beneficial-ownership confirmation (Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners) — the SCSp must annually verify and confirm the accuracy of all filed UBO data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days following the anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration; mandatory at least once in each calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250 per breach; deliberate omission or false filing carries criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years; LBR may refer the matter to the Public Prosecutor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS file renewal fee (taxe annuelle) for the commercial register dossier of the SCSp.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the RCS registration; invoice payable within 30 days of issuance.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and penalty notices; persistent non-payment triggers RCS formal warning and eventual administrative strike-off (radiation) of the entity from the Luxembourg commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax declaration for the fiscally transparent partnership, reporting the SCSp's re-invoicing profit/loss and its allocation among the general and limited partners.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg direct tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Electronic filing: 31 December of the year following the tax year (calendar-year SCSp); paper filing: 31 May of the year following the tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to EUR 25,000; default interest of 0.6% per month on any assessed amount; risk of taxation d'office (official default assessment) and heightened audit exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT declaration (Form 502) consolidating the Luxembourg B2B supplies of the re-invoicing hub; filed as the final periodic return of the VAT year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg VAT authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of the year following the VAT year for annual-basis taxpayers; monthly filers by the 12th and quarterly filers by the 20th of the month following the final period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 500 for late filing; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on due VAT; penalties for inaccurate returns and potential VAT recovery blockage by the AEDT.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent réviseur d'entreprises must be appointed where the SCSp exceeds at least two of three criteria on the balance-sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce of 50 employees. The SCSp is exempt from publication of annual accounts but remains subject to the statutory audit obligation under the Law of 23 July 2016 and Article 69 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP per the Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and accounting records and annual accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU), accounting records kept in EUR; IFRS permitted only for consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file and maintain beneficial-ownership data with the RBE and reconfirm it at least once per year, within 15 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration. Any change in limited-partner shareholding or control must be filed within 30 days of the change; the annual confirmation requires sign-off by a gérant confirming that the on-file UBO structure remains true and accurate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Registre des Associés) - statutory ledger of all general and limited partners, contributions, transfers, and holdings, kept at the registered office
Register of Gérants and Directors - record of managing partner appointments, removals, and signature rights
Minute Book - resolutions, consents, contribution approvals, and other partnership records evidencing corporate acts

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,500–8,000 per annum (market range for a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent and corporate secretarial support for a re-invoicing SCSp, excluding RBE/AML filings and professional board fees)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000–45,000 per engagement (typical Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises fee for an active re-invoicing SCSp exceeding the audit thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level (fiscally transparent); underlying partners exposed to Luxembourg CIT/income tax; the standard aggregate Luxembourg corporate headline rate for capital companies is 24.94% (Luxembourg City, 2025).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp profits allocated to partners may qualify for the Luxembourg participation exemption (exemption on substantial shareholdings) or for treaty benefits; no specific CIT incentive applies to the SCSp itself; commercial re-invoicing margins must be at arm's length and do not enjoy preferential re-invoicing tax regimes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 500 (company income tax return) and Formulaire 545 (municipal business tax) for entities subject to CIT/MBT; partnerships file declaration on Form 575 (income tax declaration for partnerships); filed via MyGuichet.lu / eCAB.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 May of the following year or 31 December in case of online filing, subject to extension requests; actual assessed basis is the calendar/fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form (SCSp), business activity (ISIC 4690 re-invoicing trade), registered office, tax number (matricule).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a fiscally transparent SCSp, non-resident partners must report the Luxembourg-sourced profits allocated to them in their own annual tax returns; the SCSp acts as an information return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income or loss of the partnership and its allocation among partners according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income allocations (e.g., through a permanent establishment of the SP).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax withheld on dividends, interest, royalties, and other Luxembourg-source income after treaty relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty withholding tax relief by attaching Form 500/WHT; submit a residence certificate (CRS) to the Luxembourg tax office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.75% of tax due per month of delay, up to 20%; additional 10% increase for lack of declaration; possible administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 and criminal sanctions for intentionally omitted income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% under the parent-subsidiary directive and domestic participation exemption when conditions met (e.g., 10% participation or 12-month holding period, EU/EEA companies).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for withholding tax relief in Luxembourg via the Form 500/WHT procedure or filing a refund claim with Luxembourg tax authorities; attach the relevant double tax treaty (DTA/TRC) and proof of beneficial ownership. If the SCSp is transparent, treaty-relief requests must reflect the residence/status of the partners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% statutory rate (0% for EU parent-subsidiary interest not classified as dividend; otherwise EU Savings Directive/general anti-abuse rules apply). Royalties: 15% statutory rate; treaty rate may be reduced to 0-10% depending on the DTA, often 0% for royalties under Luxembourg treaties.
